title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-19

ai_review.summary: Rough audience tape of a Dec 19 1973 show captures an all‑time great set—stellar “Here Comes Sunshine”, superb “Nobody’s Fault…”, a legendary Half Step and other highlights—despite water‑damaged audio.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently praised as one of the band’s finest of ’73, with standout renditions of “Here Comes Sunshine”, “West Riding Suite”, “Nobody’s Fault But Mine” and an unforgettable Half Step. Reviewers note the recording is an audience (AUD) source that suffers from heat‑ or water‑damage and occasional muffled sections, but it remains listenable enough to enjoy the epic second‑set segues. Overall sentiment is overwhelmingly positive, with the musical quality far outweighing the technical flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 5‑star ratings for the performance; only one low rating reflects audio issues. Weighted average (70 % show, 30 % recording) yields a strong 4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stealth audience tape with heat/water damage; rough and not crystal‑clear but still listenable. Some dropout/ambient noise, but captures the full show.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but uneven (notably the “Playin’” segment); second set shines with classic segues Truckin → Nobody's Fault → Jam → The Other One, delivering high‑energy jams and space meltdowns.

band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass solo is missing (disallowed before release), but his overall playing is praised as “letter perfect”.
